accepted.title: Compute exact distance in the free factor complex
accepted.text: For n≥3, let FFₙ have vertices the conjugacy classes [H] of nontrivial proper free factors H≤Fₙ, and an edge when representatives of two classes are comparable by inclusion. Is there an algorithm which, given finite generators for two free factors, returns their combinatorial distance in the 1-skeleton of FFₙ?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: Actual held PDF, pdftotext -layout physical page and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: Restrict n≥3 because the stated inclusion graph is disconnected for n=2; this is the domain in which the source connectivity assertion applies. Exact graph distance, not a coarse approximation. The distance-four special case already proved is not treated as a full answer.
accepted.literature_finding: The published 2024 paper still provides algorithms only for distances1,2,3 and4 with a codimension-one factor. Fresh exact-distance searches located no full closure.
accepted.status_grade: B: explicit primary-source question retained; bounded fresh primary-literature review, not certified open

accepted.title: Recognize the fixed subgroup of a single free-group automorphism
accepted.text: Is there an algorithm which, given n≥2 and a finite list of words generating H≤Fₙ, decides whether H=Fix(φ)={w∈Fₙ:φ(w)=w} for some single automorphism φ∈Aut(Fₙ)?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

locator.verified_from: Actual held PDF, pdftotext -layout physical page and printed footer

accepted.scope_review: Single automorphism is essential; algorithms for fixed subgroups of families, or computing Fix(φ) from φ, are distinct. All finite ranks, not merely rank3.
accepted.literature_finding: Carvalho 2023 primary introduction explicitly retains recognition for a single automorphism as undecided (Question8.6). Martino–Ventura structural description2003 is not claimed to be an effective recognition procedure. No later full algorithm located.
accepted.status_grade: B: explicit primary-source question retained; bounded fresh primary-literature review, not certified open
